newsitem.title: USA: Paris Club's Noyer sees relief before year-end.
newsitem.headline: Paris Club's Noyer sees relief before year-end.

text.p: Paris Club chairman Christian Noyer said on Saturday that he expected the creditors group to offer debt relief under new improved terms before the end of the year.
The Paris Club has agreed to offer debt relief of up to 80 percent on a case-by-case basis to poor heavily-indebted countries, compared to 67 percent currently available.

The improved debt relief is part of a joint initiative launched by the World Bank and International Monetary Fund, which will also take action to lift the burden of debt owed to them by very poor countries.
"Given the action by the IMF and World Bank, we will provide an exit rescheduling for all countries, even the most difficult," Noyer said by telephone from Paris.
Asked how quickly debt acccords would be reached under the new terms, he said, "there will be some between now and the end of the year".
France has dubbed the new debt relief "Lyon terms" after a Group of Seven summit in Lyon, France, in June, which called for greater help for the world's poorest nations.
Noyer said there was no list of countries which will benefit first from the new terms of debt relief.
But he said it was unlikely that it would be Uganda, cited by some officials in creditor nations.
"Uganda, which has already benefitted from a write-off of stock, is doing well. It is not clear that it would be a priority," he said.
